slides: Your muscles don’t remember the weight, they remember the pattern.
If you add the same load every session, the nervous system adapts and stalls.
A 2‑5% increase each week forces new fiber recruitment.
Pair that with a 48‑hour recovery window to cement the signal.
So tweak the load, not the routine, and growth becomes inevitable.
When your to‑do list mirrors your values, execution feels effortless.
Misaligned tasks drain mental bandwidth, creating resistance.
Start each morning by ranking tasks against your core purpose.
Drop or delegate anything below a 70% alignment score.
Alignment turns discipline into a natural byproduct, not a chore.
Sleep isn’t downtime; it’s the engine room of performance.
Growth hormone spikes during the first 90 minutes of deep sleep.
Disrupting that window blunts muscle repair and fat loss.
A dark, cool bedroom and a consistent bedtime protect that surge.
Prioritize the first sleep cycle, and your training pays dividends.
Momentum is the frictionless state that follows a single completed action.
Your brain registers success as a dopamine cue, priming the next move.
Set a micro‑goal that can’t fail—five push‑ups, one email.
When that micro‑goal is done, the next feels half‑as hard.
Start with the smallest win; the chain reaction builds itself.
